scope: Real web and native behaviour, calculations, persistence, ownership, offline and error handling, localisation, and date handling

execution.rule: Evidence must be executable behaviour or production source. Screenshots are not parity evidence.

areas.label: Authentication and identity
observations: Both clients keep the entry surface neutral until authentication resolves the account persona.
Private hydration and mutation work is bound to the captured authenticated owner rather than mutable global session state.
Expired or anonymous-session failures preserve queued data while bounded authentication recovery runs.

behaviour.evidence: Neutral entry, authenticated persona reveal, and account-bound session tests exist on both clients.

calculations.evidence: Identity selection has no cross-client numeric calculation.

database_reads.evidence: Profile, settings, and dashboard reads resolve under the authenticated account on both clients.

database_writes.evidence: Mutations use authenticated Supabase clients and captured owner IDs.

ownership.evidence: Account switches invalidate stale callbacks, hydration, acknowledgements, and outbox work.

offline.evidence: IndexedDB on web and account-scoped JSON on native differ mechanically but preserve the same owner-bound queue semantics.

errors.evidence: Authentication failures pause and refresh instead of silently quarantining user data.

localisation.evidence: Entry and authentication copy is covered by the offered-language contracts.

date_handling.evidence: Identity resolution is not calendar dependent.

areas.label: Offered languages
observations: Both clients offer the same nine languages: English, German, Swiss German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Romanian, and Thai.
Runtime selection, format arguments, scripts, short forms, and stranded-English guards are executable contracts rather than key-count claims.
Language resources ship locally and do not depend on network availability.

behaviour.evidence: Both selectors expose the same language set and persist the selected language.

calculations.evidence: Language selection does not alter domain calculations.

database_reads.evidence: Bundled interface copy is not read from Supabase.

database_writes.evidence: The selected language is encoded through the existing account settings contract where it is synchronized.

ownership.evidence: Language follows the active account/settings boundary rather than leaking another profile's preference.

offline.evidence: All offered interface resources are bundled with each client.

errors.evidence: Fallback and format-token checks prevent missing or malformed runtime copy.

localisation.evidence: Structural, runtime, script, format, and short-form policies cover all nine offered languages.

date_handling.evidence: Localized dates use the selected language while domain date keys remain canonical.

areas.label: Simple and Advanced modes
observations: Simple is the default for new profiles while an explicit Advanced choice remains respected.
Both modes operate on the same account dashboard and calendar records rather than maintaining parallel data models.
Workout-owned gestures do not become day navigation, and Simple completion stays bounded on empty routines.

behaviour.evidence: Mode defaulting, persistence, navigation, and shared schedule behavior are covered on both clients.

calculations.evidence: Mode changes presentation, not target or workout calculation engines.

database_reads.evidence: Both modes consume the same profile, settings, plan, nutrition, and history rows.

database_writes.evidence: Mode selection persists through the canonical settings row.

ownership.evidence: Mode and dashboard state are rebound at the account boundary.

offline.evidence: Local snapshots preserve mode and dashboard behavior until synchronization resumes.

errors.evidence: Missing or incomplete plans remain non-runnable and route back to a valid builder path.

localisation.evidence: Mode labels and their core surfaces use the common offered-language policy.

date_handling.evidence: Simple and Advanced resolve the same active profile date and calendar day.

areas.label: Date navigation and calendar
observations: Simple, Nutrition, and training use one active per-profile date context while retaining an honest real-today marker.
Copy, clear, and paste operate on valid target days, copied rows receive fresh identities, and repeated intent remains idempotent.
Configured meal timezone owns day rollover instead of the device's incidental current zone.

behaviour.evidence: Navigation, deliberate swipe, prescription, empty-day, and copy/clear/paste behavior are executable on both clients.

calculations.evidence: Day selection is a canonical date-key calculation with the same timezone boundary.

database_reads.evidence: Both clients scope dashboard and calendar reads to the selected date or an explicit bounded range.

database_writes.evidence: Copied records use new UUIDs while idempotency keys prevent duplicate copy intent.

ownership.evidence: Saved active dates and copied calendar rows are profile scoped.

offline.evidence: Calendar edits remain visible from local snapshots and replay through owner-bound queues.

errors.evidence: Invalid paste targets and incomplete prescriptions are rejected rather than silently creating bad days.

localisation.evidence: Calendar actions and date presentation are covered in offered-language resources.

date_handling.evidence: Explicit route date, saved profile date, today marker, timezone rollover, and Gregorian HealthKit boundaries are tested.

areas.label: Nutrition at a Glance and target modal
observations: Both clients expose the same calories and macro targets from the shared activity, goal, and calibration facts.
Target changes recalculate calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate together rather than editing one display number.
The glance surface remains a summary and the target editor owns explicit goal changes.

behaviour.evidence: Glance, target editing, preset selection, and macro-detail behavior are covered by production tests.

calculations.evidence: Golden engine fixtures and target tests compare calories, macros, activity, and calibration values.

database_reads.evidence: Profile, settings, daily log, activity, and food totals hydrate the same target model.

database_writes.evidence: Goal, nutrition mode, and target preferences persist through canonical settings/daily contracts.

ownership.evidence: Targets are calculated from the active profile and never another account's body or activity facts.

offline.evidence: The latest local settings and daily facts remain authoritative while writes are pending.

errors.evidence: Missing measured BMR and incomplete activity facts use bounded documented fallbacks.

localisation.evidence: Glance, target, goal, and macro copy is part of the nine-language runtime contract.

date_handling.evidence: Daily targets and consumed totals resolve against the shared active date.

areas.label: Daily Activity Estimator
observations: Quick mode applies one explicit PAL multiplier; Precise mode sums attributable activity above the sedentary floor.
Whole-day wearable burn supersedes overlapping estimates, while run distance and discounted watch calories deduplicate with max instead of sum.
Measured BMR is authoritative and safety floors remain bounded across both clients.

behaviour.evidence: Quick and Precise modes remain distinct choices and present their own inputs.

calculations.evidence: The fitness-brain golden fixture and activity tests pin PAL, MET, BMR, wearable, goal, and macro outputs.

database_reads.evidence: Activity catalogue, profile body facts, health metrics, and daily logs feed the same calculation contract.

database_writes.evidence: Selected estimator mode and activity facts use canonical settings/activity rows.

ownership.evidence: Shared catalogue METs are applied to the active profile's weight and owner-scoped activity only.

offline.evidence: Local estimator inputs and queued activity edits calculate without a server round trip.

errors.evidence: Missing, absurd, or overlapping inputs fall back or deduplicate instead of inflating expenditure.

localisation.evidence: Mode, activity, PAL, and guidance copy is localized through the common policy.

date_handling.evidence: Precise activity is day-owned and late wearable facts reconcile into that same date.

areas.label: Meal composer and Food Memory
observations: Both clients preserve immutable meal snapshots, exact amounts, presets, history ranking, and fresh row identities when a preset is applied.
Food Memory ranks real prior entries by meal block, weekday, time, frequency, and recency without surfacing synthetic prescriptions.
Meal replacement, remembered amounts, and outbox intents are atomic and account scoped.

behaviour.evidence: Compose, configure, quick add, barcode, history, preset, edit, delete, and undo behavior is covered.

calculations.evidence: Golden Food Memory, macro guidance, portion, hydration, and draft-total tests compare actual outputs.

database_reads.evidence: Foods, meals, entries, preferences, and presets paginate and hydrate without catalogue-reference loss.

database_writes.evidence: Atomic meal RPCs and canonical preset payloads preserve immutable snapshots and idempotency.

ownership.evidence: Async commits, hydration, preferences, and outboxes are bound to the account that started them.

offline.evidence: Queued replacement tombstones and local snapshots stay authoritative during reconnect.

errors.evidence: Only safe missing optional references detach; permanent failures remain visible and valid later operations continue.

localisation.evidence: Composer, units, presets, history, scanner, and error copy are included in runtime localization tests.

date_handling.evidence: Meal local date, finished-at time, configured timezone, daily memory, and same-weekday memory are explicit.

areas.label: Hydration
observations: Both clients keep one attributable ledger for drinks, food water, and external facts while exact custom targets override automatic drift.
Automatic targets use body size and bounded exercise; late wearable values only corroborate within caps.
Account, day, idempotency key, and revision prevent duplicate or foreign hydration from entering the visible total.

behaviour.evidence: Quick add, custom amount, presets, history, deletion, target modes, and visible composition are covered.

calculations.evidence: Food-water derivation, target bounds, portion scaling, ledger totals, and composition proportions are pinned.

database_reads.evidence: Hydration events, preferences, food water, activity, and health facts hydrate under the same owner/day contract.

database_writes.evidence: Stable per-account/day sync IDs and revisioned event writes are canonical across clients.

ownership.evidence: Foreign accounts, delayed watch mutations, and account changes cannot cross the active hydration boundary.

offline.evidence: Local ledger mutations overlay remote snapshots and replay without resurrecting deletes.

errors.evidence: Empty or partial wearable reads never erase persisted hydration; invalid targets are rejected.

localisation.evidence: Units, presets, history, editor, and target copy are included in the offered-language runtime contract.

date_handling.evidence: Ledger rows and automatic targets are owner/day scoped and rebase at midnight.

areas.label: Supplements
observations: Simple and Nutrition use one supplement-stack model on both clients.
Browse order leads with protein and creatine, then remains alphabetical.
Retiring a supplement removes it from the active stack without deleting historical logs.

behaviour.evidence: Browse, add, edit, log, and retire behavior uses one stack model across surfaces.

calculations.evidence: Dose and display derivations use the same canonical catalogue fields; no client invents an independent nutrition calculation.

database_reads.evidence: Stack items, catalogue metadata, and historical logs hydrate through canonical rows.

database_writes.evidence: Composite supplement log keys and deduplicated batches match the production contract.

ownership.evidence: Stacks and logs are account scoped while catalogue facts are shared.

offline.evidence: Local stack edits and logs remain visible while their owner-bound writes are pending.

errors.evidence: Duplicate batches are normalized before write and retiring never destroys history.

localisation.evidence: Names, groups, guidance, editor, and popup labels are covered in every offered language.

date_handling.evidence: Supplement logs retain their account date and historical ordering.

areas.label: Recovery and wearables
observations: Recovery, external-session credit, wearable deduplication, and nutrition timing consume the same recorded facts and bounded rules.
Native reads HealthKit and Apple Fitness directly; web accepts synchronized/manual wearable facts because browsers cannot access HealthKit.
Partial or denied native health queries preserve readable facts and cancellation never publishes a partial snapshot.

behaviour.evidence: Recovery output is shared, but direct HealthKit permission and query behavior exists only on Apple platforms.

calculations.evidence: Session contribution, fatigue, recovery, meal timing, and wearable deduplication rules are pinned across clients.

database_reads.evidence: Both clients read the same synchronized health metrics, activities, daily logs, and recovery facts.

database_writes.evidence: Imported activities and health metrics use canonical UUID, source, owner, and date fields.

ownership.evidence: Health and recovery facts are filtered to the active owner; manual entries remain authoritative.

offline.evidence: Last readable facts survive offline/partial refresh and imported writes replay through owner-bound queues.

errors.evidence: Native distinguishes denied, empty, partial, failed, and cancelled HealthKit reads; web has no HealthKit permission state.

localisation.evidence: Recovery, wearable, and external-session guidance is localized on both clients.

date_handling.evidence: Health summaries, sleep, workouts, recovery, and meal timing resolve by canonical local day.

areas.label: Avatar and visual progress
observations: Both clients share pose-aware selection, crop geometry, comparison timing, storage paths, snapshot timing, strength comparison, and export content.
Browser and native camera lifecycles differ by platform; native additionally supports depth placement and hardware shutter controls.
Private uploads are owner scoped, retry safely, and surface recoverable storage errors.

behaviour.evidence: Capture, gallery, compare, and export are shared; depth and hardware volume shutter behavior are native-only capabilities.

calculations.evidence: Golden progress fixtures compare crop, pose, elapsed days, snapshot selection, poster content, and strength calculations.

database_reads.evidence: Photo metadata, body snapshots, training history, and private storage hydrate under one owner contract.

database_writes.evidence: Deterministic private paths, photo metadata, and delete tombstones use the same production model.

ownership.evidence: Unsafe owner paths are rejected and account switches hide stale private media.

offline.evidence: Upload queues deduplicate retries and hydrate pending edits/deletes over stale remote rows.

errors.evidence: Both surface recoverable storage errors; camera/depth failure modes follow their platform APIs.

localisation.evidence: Capture, framing, comparison, assessment, trend, and recommendation copy is covered by offered-language tests.

date_handling.evidence: Capture timestamps and on-or-before body snapshots prevent future data from entering a comparison.

areas.label: Orbit
observations: Campaign generation, route facts, stable imported-activity UUIDs, cross-domain proposals, reconciliation, and privacy exports share canonical contracts.
Native uses CoreLocation and native route presentation; web uses browser geolocation and its own map renderer.
Server pagination and pending edits/deletes reconcile without losing local Orbit changes.

behaviour.evidence: Mission, campaign, library, run, and proposal behavior is shared; map and location acquisition use platform-native APIs.

calculations.evidence: Stable IDs, route scoring, run metrics, campaign phasing, Avatar contribution, and fueling proposals are pinned.

database_reads.evidence: Orbit hydration paginates all ordered rows and consumes canonical run, route, campaign, and activity data.

database_writes.evidence: Database-safe deterministic UUIDs and canonical imported activity/source fields are used by both clients.

ownership.evidence: Pending checks, hydration, reconciliation, and privacy archives are owner scoped.

offline.evidence: Queued edits and deletes overlay remote snapshots and acknowledgements preserve newer local work.

errors.evidence: Both reject invalid geometry and stale data; location permission errors follow CoreLocation or browser geolocation.

localisation.evidence: Orbit presentation and guidance use each client's offered-language runtime.

date_handling.evidence: Runs, campaigns, imported activities, and cross-domain proposals retain explicit timestamps and local dates.

areas.label: Settings
observations: Mode, language, timezone, weight unit, meal-memory cadence, hydration, and account preferences use the canonical settings row.
Weight-unit changes alter display only and never rewrite stored kilograms.
Native additionally owns Apple permission and device-integration settings that have no browser equivalent.

behaviour.evidence: Shared account preferences behave alike; HealthKit, notifications, Watch, and other Apple integrations are native-only settings.

calculations.evidence: Unit conversion and settings-derived mode/target behavior preserve canonical stored values.

database_reads.evidence: Both clients hydrate one owner-scoped settings row and safely default newly additive fields.

database_writes.evidence: Settings updates use canonical snake_case fields and singleton conflict behavior.

ownership.evidence: Settings rebind to the authenticated profile and queued singleton settings cannot leak across accounts.

offline.evidence: Pending singleton settings remain authoritative during reconnect hydration.

errors.evidence: Shared validation is aligned; Apple permission failures exist only in the native client.

localisation.evidence: Shared settings labels, choices, actions, and errors follow the nine-language contract.

date_handling.evidence: Timezone selection explicitly controls meal/day rollover while absolute persisted timestamps remain unchanged.
